claim: A line whose first token is not one of v160.7's statement mnemonics is not an instruction at all: the parser builds an InvalidStatement for it, so the line shows as noop and never runs (the rest of the program still compiles).
why: LParser.java:142-147 wraps `LogicIO.read(tokens, tok)` in try/catch and substitutes `new InvalidStatement()` on any exception -- an unknown mnemonic is not in LogicIO's table, so it throws and the line becomes a noop. The whitelist is the @RegisterStatement set extracted from the v160.7 jar (LStatements.java, 54 names: noop read write draw print ... playsound playmusic setmarker makemarker localeprint), which is exactly the set stored as INSTR_SPECS. Mnemonics are case-sensitive: real-engine probes (out/_noop_matrix2.py, out/_probe_extra.py) returned InvalidStatement for `RADAR enemy any any distance turret1 1 out`, `END` and `NOOP`, while the lowercase spellings were real statements. Comments (`# ...`) and label lines (`name:`) are stripped before this check and blank lines are skipped.
